title: Observability ingest snags - cribsheet
content:
Quick brain-dump / running notebook for the ingest drop that started ~2026-02-24 16:10 UTC.

Background (TL;DR):
- Around 2026-02-24 16:10 UTC we observed a ~60% drop in log ingest rate to the observability pipeline (Logstash/Filebeat -> Kafka -> OTEL-Collector -> ES). Traces were partial: many spans missing service.name or dropped entirely. Metrics ingestion (Prom/Pushgateway) largely unaffected.
- Affected customers: internal canaries + a handful of early Dedicated tenants.
- Pattern: sudden drop, then intermittent bursts, never full recovery without manual intervention.

What I observed (timeline):
- 2026-02-24 16:07 UTC: alert firing CPU on otel-collector-0 (node 4) but CPU only 65%.
- 2026-02-24 16:10 UTC: logs ingestion rate drops (see quick grep below).
- 2026-02-24 17:00 UTC: I toggled a rolling restart on otel-collector ds in staging -> small improvement.
- 2026-02-25 09:30 UTC: found repeated errors in collector: "failed to encode export request: resource not found" (snippet later).
- 2026-02-25 11:00 UTC: increased kafka consumer parallelism (consumer-group scaling) — temporary bump.

Commands/traces I ran (copy-pasta):
- kafka consumer lag check:
  kubectl exec -it deploy/kafka-tools -- /bin/sh -c "kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --describe --group obs-ingest"
  -> consumer lag stayed low for most topics, but topic obs-raw-logs had 30-40% lower throughput.

- tail Collector logs (filtered):
  kubectl -n observability logs ds/otel-collector -c otel-collector --since=2h | egrep "error|warn|drop|failed" -n | sed -n '1,200p'
  sample lines: 
    [2026-02-25T09:29:58Z] WARN exporterhelper/queued_retry.go: Retrying export failed: failed to encode export request: resource not found
    [2026-02-25T09:30:01Z] ERROR pipeline/trace: failed to send batch, status=UNAVAILABLE
    [2026-02-25T09:31:20Z] WARN exporter/logging.go: Dropping 120 spans due to queue limit reached

- otel-collector config diff (recent deploy):
  git show --name-only origin/main:deploy/otel-collector.yaml | sed -n '1,200p'
  noticed: sampling processor added (rate limiting), queue_size reduced from 5000 -> 500, batching timeout changed from 200ms -> 50ms.

- Heap/FDs on collector pods:
  kubectl exec -it otel-collector-0 -- sh -c "ps aux | grep otel && cat /proc/$(pidof otelcol)/limits"
  -> no obvious fd exhaustion, RSS ~420MB (expected), but open files ~1024 (we typically run at 4096) -> ah, limits lowered.

- Quick ES error scan (ingest index write errors):
  curl -s -u es-user:XXXX 'https://es.internal/_cat/indices?v' | egrep obs-ingest
  -> obs-raw-logs-2026.02.24 yellow, docs count stalled, health changed to yellow around 16:12 UTC.

Hypotheses (brainstorm):
1) Otel-Collector config change (queue/batch/sampler) increased dropped spans under transient backpressure -> manifests as low ingest and drop warnings.
2) Elasticsearch shard issues (unassigned primaries) causing exporter to see UNAVAILABLE -> Collector retries and queue overflows.
3) Kafka broker throttle or network egress bottleneck between Filebeat -> Kafka causing flow control; rarer because kafka lag didn't spike.
4) New sidecar (envoy) version rolled to nodes with default ulimit=1024 that reduced file descriptors so collectors hit queue limits sooner.
5) OTLP exporter auth token rotated and some pods stuck with old token -> 401-like errors masked as resource not found.

Error snippets (copied):
- "failed to encode export request: resource not found" (Collector exporterhelper)
- "Dropping 120 spans due to queue limit reached"
- "write failed, transport error: context deadline exceeded" (ES client)
- "bulk request conflicts: index primaries unassigned" (ES bulk response)

Quick experiments attempted and outcomes: (notes to self)
- Increase otel-collector queue_size to 2500 in a canary -> immediate reduction in drop warnings but spikes in pod memory usage.
- Temporarily redirect a small percentage (~5%) of logs to a fallback ES cluster (read-replica) -> those logs indexed fine, implies ES primary cluster partial issue.
- Recovered one affected node by raising ulimit via daemonset -> collector on node had fewer drop messages but not full recovery cluster-wide.

Observations about sampling & batching config: 
- The recent change (batch.timeout 50ms) was intended to reduce latency but likely increases number of small batches and higher exporter pressure -> with ES backpressure this amplifies.
- sampling: tail-based sampler with lower threshold (5 spans) might be promoting more spans to be exported than before.

Immediate next steps (practical):
- TODO: Revert batch.timeout to 200ms in canary and monitor drop logs (owner: Aisha) (JIRA: JIRA-OPS-9876-A)
- TODO: Open ES incident with infra team, share bulk error sample and time window (owner: Ethan)
- TODO: Check KMS token rotation logs for otel exporter secrets on 2026-02-24 15:45-16:10 UTC (owner: Priya)
- TODO: Add exporter's retry_on_http_5xx backoff jitter to reduce synchronized retries (owner: Aisha)
- TODO: Add an alert specifically for "Dropping .* spans due to queue limit reached" to fire before downstream SLO impact (owner: eng-observability)

Longer term notes (ideas):
- Add a small local filesystem ring buffer for spans when exporter returns UNAVAILABLE (fallback to disk) to smooth spikes.
- Add a single-sample telemetry endpoint on collectors to expose queue length, dropped_count, export_err_rate per 10s to Grafana.
- Revisit default ulimits in base node images and enforce via clusterpolicy.

Random commands / snippets to re-run next time (for my notes):
- kubectl -n observability exec -it ds/otel-collector -- cat /etc/otel-collector/config.yaml | sed -n '1,300p'
- tcpdump -i eth0 port 4317 -w /tmp/otlp-dump.pcap (on affected node) then scp for offline analysis
- curl -s 'https://es.internal/_cluster/allocation/explain' -u es-user:XXXX | jq '.'

Unresolved questions (notes to chase in meetings):
- Which rollout touched collectors/sidecars on 2026-02-24 15:30-16:00? (release-engineering changelog?)
- Any infra autoscaling or maintenance windows at that time? (cloud provider ops?)
- Did any tenant push a huge trace fanout / noisy instrumentation that triggered tail-sampling behavior around that time? (solutions-eng to check)

Notes to self: keep this doc rough. If we find the root cause we can consolidate into a Confluence postmortem template. For now, capture steps that reproduced the symptom and the commands above so I don't forget the manual checks.

End of cribsheet.
